Handle unusual __qualname__ in inspect

## Checklist

- [x] I've run the latest [black](https://github.com/psf/black) with default args on new code.
- [x] I've updated CHANGELOG.md and CONTRIBUTORS.md where appropriate (see note about typos above).
- [x] I've added tests for new code.
- [x] I accept that @willmcgugan may be pedantic in the code review.

## Description

I discovered, that an object with an unusual `__qualname__` attribute (not a `str`, e.g. a descriptor) causes `inspect` to fail.
This can happen if an object is created this way intentionally, but I discovered it, when decorating a class with `@functools.lru_cache` which forwards the underlying attributes using a descriptor when it can't add the to it's `__dict__` because the class uses `__slots__`:

```python
from functools import lru_cache
from rich import inspect


@lru_cache
class Klaas:
    __slots__ = ("__qualname__",)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    from rich.traceback import install

    install()

    inspect(Klaas.__qualname__)
    inspect(Klaas, all=True)
```

I fixed it by checking the type of `__qualname__` falling back to `__name__` and if that isn't a `str` using the already provided fallback.

FILES: rich/_inspect.py:103-103
ROOT CAUSE: The `_get_signature` method in `rich/_inspect.py` uses `getattr(obj, "__qualname__", name)` without verifying that the result is a string. In some cases, such as when a class is decorated with `@lru_cache` and uses `__slots__`, `__qualname__` can be a descriptor (e.g., `member_descriptor`), which causes `Text.assemble` to fail with a `TypeError`.
CHANGE: Modify line 103 to verify that `__qualname__` is a string, falling back to `__name__` if it is not, and finally to `name`.
Specifically, change:
`qualname = name or getattr(obj, "__qualname__", name)`
to:
`qualname = getattr(obj, "__qualname__", name)`
`if not isinstance(qualname, str):`
`    qualname = getattr(obj, "__name__", name)`
`if not isinstance(qualname, str):`
`    qualname = name`
(Or a more concise equivalent that ensures `qualname` is a string).
TEST: Run `python3 reproduce_issue.py` to verify the fix. Also run `pytest tests/test_inspect.py`.

steps.message:
I have fixed the issue where `rich.inspect` would fail if an object had a `__qualname__` that was not a string (e.g., a descriptor). This occurred specifically in cases like classes decorated with `@lru_cache` using `__slots__`.

I modified `rich/_inspect.py` in the `_get_signature` method to explicitly verify that `qualname` is a string, falling back to `__name__` and then to the provided `name` if necessary.

```python
# rich/_inspect.py
qualname = getattr(obj, "__qualname__", name)
if not isinstance(qualname, str):
    qualname = getattr(obj, "__name__", name)
if not isinstance(qualname, str):
    qualname = name
```

Verified the fix with `reproduce_issue.py`.

steps.message:
The issue where `rich.inspect` would fail when an object had a non-string `__qualname__` (such as a member descriptor in classes decorated with `@lru_cache` using `__slots__`) has been resolved. I verified that the fix in `rich/_inspect.py` correctly handles these cases by validating the type of `qualname` and falling back to `__name__` or a default name when necessary.

The fix was applied as follows:
```python
        qualname = getattr(obj, "__qualname__", name)
        if not isinstance(qualname, str):
            qualname = getattr(obj, "__name__", name)
        if not isinstance(qualname, str):
            qualname = name
```
I confirmed the fix using a reproduction script that specifically triggered the described failure.
